label: Town of Brattleboro
header:
# Town of Brattleboro municipal roster backfill -- Vermont
# municipal fan-out batch 3; issue #163 (VT master tracking).

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Selectboard Members' directory (updated June 5, 2026): lists five Brattleboro Selectboard members: Peter Case, Amanda Ellis-Thurber (Vice Chair), Isaac Evans-Frantz, Oscar Heller (Chair), and Eleanor Mayo.

Town of Brattleboro, official March 3, 2026 election results (published by the Town Clerk): Amanda Ellis-Thurber (1,556) won the three-year seat and Isaac Evans-Frantz (1,462) and Eleanor Mayo (1,255) won the one-year seats filled in 2026.
Town of Brattleboro charter, 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 107, section 2.2 (official text): section 2.2(2) provides for a Selectboard of five members elected at large.
Town of Brattleboro charter, 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 107, section 2.2 (official text): section 2.2(7) provides for the election of a Moderator for a one-year term.
Town of Brattleboro, official March 3, 2026 election results (published by the Town Clerk): David Gartenstein (1,911) won the Moderator contest in 2026.
Town of Brattleboro charter, 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 107, section 2.2 (official text): section 2.2(5) provides for a Board of three listers elected at large, one each year for three-year terms.
Town of Brattleboro 2025-2026 Annual Report, 'Town Officers' (report p. 6): lists the Board of Listers as Katherine Dowd (term to 2027), Heidi Fischer (term to 2028), and Tom Franks (term to 2026).
Town of Brattleboro, official March 3, 2026 election results (published by the Town Clerk): Thomas "Tom" Franks (1,749) was re-elected Lister (three-year term) in 2026.
Town of Brattleboro charter, 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 107, section 2.2 (official text): section 2.2(6) provides for three trustees of public funds elected at large, one each year for three-year terms.

Town of Brattleboro 2025-2026 Annual Report, 'Town Officers' (report p. 6): lists the Trustees of Public Funds as Deborah Zak (term to 2027), Pamela Matweecha (term to 2028), and Katherine "Kate" John (term to 2026).

Town of Brattleboro, official March 3, 2026 election results (published by the Town Clerk): Catherine "Kate" John (1,698) was re-elected Trustee of Public Funds (three-year term) in 2026. The two town sources differ on her full first name (Katherine/Catherine); the common form Kate John is recorded.
Town of Brattleboro charter, 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 107, section 2.2 (official text): section 2.2(7) provides for the election of a First Constable for a one-year term.

Town of Brattleboro, official March 3, 2026 election results (published by the Town Clerk): Gary Corey (1,642) won the First Constable contest in 2026 (the 2025-2026 Annual Report showed the first constable seat vacant and Corey as Second Constable before the election).
Town of Brattleboro charter, 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 107, section 2.2 (official text): section 2.2(7) provides for the election of a Second Constable for a one-year term.

Town of Brattleboro, official March 3, 2026 election results (published by the Town Clerk): the 2026 Second Constable contest had no candidate and no declared write-in winner, so no holder is recorded.

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, '2025-2026 Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists fifteen Brattleboro justices of the peace: Jane Buckingham, Franklin Chrisco, Diane Cooke, Richard Cooke, Ian Goodnow, Peter Gould, William "Bill" Harvey, Martha Healey-Nelson, Thomas "Tom" Kuralt, John Lightfoot, Lee Madden, Mary "Beverly" Miller, Kate O'Connor, Robert Oeser, and Veronica Wheelock.

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, '2025-2026 Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists fifteen Brattleboro justices of the peace for the 2025-2026 term; they are the winners of the November 5, 2024 election for the office. The listing publishes no vote totals and no party designations for justices of the peace.
